searchText: Does anyone know what EthGasStation and GasNow are planning related to EIP1559? Has anyone talked to them? In addition, does anyone have any input on the way the Mempool will behave after 1559? Notably, will it drop transactions whose basefee is unsufficient? Yes, there have been several community calls with companies in the ecosystem regarding eip1559, I'm not sure if GasStation and GasNow attended. Maybe <@!552133098075193354> can fill in the blanks Regarding the mempool, yes transactions with insufficient basefee will eventually be dropped (just as outpriced transactions right now), but (at least geth's) txpool will keep underpriced transactions in as long as possible, for a writeup of the txpool changes see: https://gist.github.com/zsfelfoldi/9607ad248707a925b701f49787904fd6 Thanks. I could not find it on the internet. It might be useful for Tim could do a thread about it. Just a quick recap on what Eth projects should expect right after the fork Those services should be largely unnecessary in a post-1559 world. Useful just as an FYI to external users, but giving useful/good gas pricing suggestions to users should be so trivial that we no longer need external complex oracles. I know but a certain number of infra that needs to be migrated are dependant on those So if the APIs are not longer supported, for instance, we will have to rewrite this part of our backend Probably not much work but still need to be addressed in the intervale I still do not understand why after 1559 miners tip is so predictable that services like gas station will be not necessary anymore. These services can continue to work as they do today, without any changes to them. They will continue to serve users who are submitting legacy transactions. I can't wait to see 1559 in action to understand Initially, miners will likely set a static minimum premium that is stable for the run of the miner. In theory, some miners may *choose* to write a "smarter" algorithm that adjusts based on a block's value (where high extractable value blocks are worth more) in which case the minimum priority fee may fluctuate from block to block. Even in the case where miners develop optimizing algorithms, we don't *expect* for the minimum miner premium (based on historic data and assumption of rational miners) to fluctuate by more than 1-5 nanoeth / gas. In all cases, we suspect there will be an equilibrium reached pretty quickly that doesn't change a lot with time (nothing like gas prices of today). Ok I definitely miss something in how 1559 works, I thought that miners can use tip to prioritize tx more or less as today, in case of congestion. The way I understand it is that in the normal regime (when base fee is not changing due to increase in incoming transactions) the tip that users set doesn’t really change anything (since the base fee makes sure your tx gets included). That’s why it’s expected that most user will default their tip to minimum. <@433705373070000138> this talk https://youtu.be/ndNyx-Oj9Wk really explains 1559 well, it’s definitely worth the time. Only during times of **changing** congestion. Specifically, when the demand for blockspace increases by more than 2x between two blocks. The system will automatically adjust to any level of demand for blockspace, but it can only adjust at a maximum speed. If the change in demand is greater than the adjustment rate, then we will end up with a small number of blocks where the gas premium is used for sorting and exclusion of the lowest. These situations are expected to be rare, and when they happen they are expected to be short lived. We'll know more on their frequency and duration after launch.

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content:
Yes, there have been several community calls with companies in the ecosystem regarding eip1559, I'm not sure if GasStation and GasNow attended.
Maybe <@!552133098075193354> can fill in the blanks
Regarding the mempool, yes transactions with insufficient basefee will eventually be dropped (just as outpriced transactions right now), but (at least geth's) txpool will keep underpriced transactions in as long as possible, for a writeup of the txpool changes see: https://gist.github.com/zsfelfoldi/9607ad248707a925b701f49787904fd6

excerpts.content: Thanks. I could not find it on the internet. It might be useful for Tim could do a thread about it. Just a quick recap on what Eth projects should expect right after the fork
